page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-32-lssd is a memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a large L3 cache of 504 MB, alongside 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 caches. The system is equipped with 248.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.75 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as 1745 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across five drives, while no dedicated GPUs are present.

Performance benchmarks reveal top-tier capabilities in single-core operations, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 53228.41 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 18257.0. The hardware excels in memory-intensive tasks, achieving a read-only small block cached memory bandwidth of 2702.38 GB/sec. Advanced instruction support is extensive, featuring Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, which assist in cryptographic and vector calculations. This is reflected in strong PassMark encryption test results and efficient LLM inference speeds, particularly for small model text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server delivers high resource density by combining substantial memory capacity with fast local NVMe storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments. However, the lack of GPU acceleration limits its utility for heavy deep learning training workloads. The instance is highly suited for memory-intensive and storage-dependent workloads, such as in-memory databases, Redis deployments, large-scale text and image processing, and high-throughput web serving.
